# Evaluation report (generated by `python -m src.model`; read it, then edit it)

## Split and method
- Held-out set: snapshots 2025-07-01, 2025-10-01 x 80 transformers (random 20%, seed 42, stratified by failed-ever / tested-ever): 160 rows, 9 failure rows. Used once.
- Development set: the other transformers at snapshots whose 12-month label ends before the first held-out snapshot: 960 rows, 38 failure rows.
- Validation: transformers shuffled into 5 groups; train on the other groups at EARLIER snapshots, validate on the group; 5 repeats, seeds 42..46; metrics are mean (range over repeats).
- All imputation and scaling sit inside a scikit-learn Pipeline, fitted on training rows only.

## Metric definitions
PR-AUC: area under precision-recall (the right headline for rare events; no-skill level equals the failure rate). Top-10% recall: share of real failures in the riskiest 10% of rows. Lift: that share divided by 0.10. Brier: mean squared error of the probabilities (lower is better).

## Comparison on development data (time-aware grouped CV)

| Model | Missing data | PR-AUC mean (range) | Top-10% recall | Brier | No-oil-test PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| age_only | - | 0.105 (0.088 to 0.123) | 0.23 | 0.0392 | 0.148 |
| health_index | - | 0.060 (0.053 to 0.066) | 0.13 | 0.0410 | 0.068 |
| logreg | median | 0.082 (0.060 to 0.103) | 0.20 | 0.1715 | 0.139 |
| logreg | median_indicator | 0.079 (0.059 to 0.100) | 0.19 | 0.1680 | 0.140 |
| hgb | native | 0.072 (0.048 to 0.086) | 0.16 | 0.1025 | 0.084 |

Chosen: **logreg + median** (simplest model within one repeat-spread of the best PR-AUC).
**Verdict against the age-only baseline in CV: the chosen model does NOT beat it (mean PR-AUC 0.082 vs 0.105).** A complex model must earn its place; say this plainly in the demo whichever way it falls.

## Final held-out result (used once)

| Model | PR-AUC [90% CI] | Top-10% recall | Lift | Brier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Age only | 0.152 [0.052, 0.406] | 0.33 | 3.33 | 0.0516 |
| Rule health index | 0.356 [0.054, 0.711] | 0.33 | 3.33 | 0.0485 |
| Final, uncalibrated | 0.096 [0.035, 0.223] | 0.11 | 1.11 | 0.1824 |
| **Final, calibrated** | 0.104 [0.038, 0.224] | 0.11 | 1.11 | 0.0528 |

Failure rows in the held-out set: 9 of 160. Intervals come from resampling whole transformers.

## Calibration
Brier before calibration 0.1824, after 0.0528. Reliability curve: `reports/reliability.png`. Calibration matters because risk = probability x impact: a systematically wrong probability changes which transformers win the budget.

## Units without an oil test
PR-AUC 0.077 [0.050, 0.260] from 1 failure rows (62 rows). They are always `scored_low_confidence` with no health score.

Median 90% range width: no oil test 0.121 vs with oil test 0.071 -> wider for untested units, as intended.

Importance shows what the model uses, not what causes failures.

## Budget test (held-out snapshot)
- Snapshot 2025-10-01, 80 units, budget scaled to 1,000,000.
- Model plan (1 replacements, 65 inspections, cost 1,000,000): removes 5,256 risk (10.0% of the units' total) and reveals up to 75,876 hidden risk for the next plan to act on.
- Age plan (4 replacements, cost 1,000,000): removes 1,202 risk (2.3%).
- For reference, a replace-only knapsack would remove 10,665 (20.3%): the gap is what the inspections cost in risk removed this year, in exchange for looking at untested and uncertain units.
- Only replacements remove risk. Inspections reveal it; their results return through /ingest and the next plan acts on them.
- Real failures among units each plan acted on: model plan 4, age plan 2.

## Timing
Training the final model: 4.7 s. Scoring with intervals: 13.02 ms per transformer.

## Honest limits
Few failures mean wide intervals; results on synthetic data describe the synthetic world; the held-out set is small. Read the final table before claiming the model beats the baselines.
